mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines a multinational corporation (MNC)?

options.A: A company that operates only within one country
options.B: A company that has its headquarters in one country but conducts production or services in two or more countries
options.C: A non‑profit organization that works across borders
options.D: A small local business with a single outlet

mcqs.answer: A company that has its headquarters in one country but conducts production or services in two or more countries
mcqs.explanation: Option B correctly defines an MNC as a company whose headquarters are in one nation but it carries out production, services, or sales in multiple other nations. Options A, C and D describe domestic firms, NGOs, or local businesses, which are not multinational corporations.

mcqs.question: When a multinational corporation decides where to invest, which factor is most likely to influence its decision?

options.A: The colour of the national flag
options.B: Availability of skilled labour and favourable market conditions
options.C: The number of tourist attractions in the country

mcqs.answer: Availability of skilled labour and favourable market conditions
mcqs.explanation: MNCs evaluate factors such as skilled labour, market size, infrastructure, political stability and policy environment when choosing investment locations. The other options are irrelevant to investment decisions.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a production partnership from a simple supplier relationship?

options.A: In a production partnership, firms share risks, investments and technology, whereas a supplier relationship involves only the sale of raw materials
options.B: A supplier relationship always involves joint ownership of factories
options.C: Production partnerships never involve any profit sharing
options.D: Supplier relationships require firms to be from the same country

mcqs.answer: In a production partnership, firms share risks, investments and technology, whereas a supplier relationship involves only the sale of raw materials
mcqs.explanation: A production partnership is collaborative: firms pool resources, share risks and technology. A simple supplier relationship is transactional, limited to supplying inputs. Options B, C and D misrepresent the nature of these arrangements.

mcqs.question: Outsourcing by a multinational corporation typically involves:

options.A: Transferring a business process to an external firm in another country to reduce costs
options.B: Hiring only local employees for all functions

mcqs.answer: Transferring a business process to an external firm in another country to reduce costs
mcqs.explanation: Outsourcing means contracting out a function to an external provider, often abroad, to achieve cost efficiency or focus on core activities. The other options describe domestic hiring, closure, or exclusive domestic investment, which are not outsourcing.

mcqs.question: Which of the following illustrates a global supply chain of a multinational corporation?

options.A: A company designs smartphones in the USA, manufactures components in South Korea, assembles them in Vietnam, and sells worldwide
options.B: A local bakery sells only within its town
options.C: A farmer sells produce only at a nearby market
options.D: A domestic car manufacturer sources all parts from within the same country

mcqs.answer: A company designs smartphones in the USA, manufactures components in South Korea, assembles them in Vietnam, and sells worldwide
mcqs.explanation: The scenario shows design, component production, assembly across three different countries and global sales – a classic global supply chain. Options B, C and D describe purely domestic or local operations.

mcqs.question: Company X is headquartered in Germany, has manufacturing plants in Mexico and China, and sells its products in over 50 countries. Which term best describes Company X?
mcqs.explanation: Company X operates in multiple countries with a headquarters in one nation, fitting the definition of a multinational corporation. The other terms refer to different organisational types.

mcqs.question: A common misconception is that multinational corporations invest in foreign countries solely to exploit cheap labour. Which statement corrects this view?

options.A: They invest only to take advantage of low wages, ignoring other factors
options.B: Investment decisions also consider market potential, political stability, infrastructure and the legal environment
options.D: They avoid countries with skilled labour

mcqs.answer: Investment decisions also consider market potential, political stability, infrastructure and the legal environment
mcqs.explanation: MNCs evaluate a range of factors—market size, political risk, infrastructure, legal frameworks, and labour costs—when investing abroad. Options A, C and D perpetuate the misconception or are inaccurate.

mcqs.question: If two firms from different countries form a production partnership to co‑develop a new product, which outcome is most likely?

options.A: Both firms will have to abandon their own R&D departments
options.B: The partnership can combine complementary technologies, reducing time to market
options.C: The partnership will eliminate all competition in the market
options.D: The firms will be forced to merge into a single legal entity

mcqs.answer: The partnership can combine complementary technologies, reducing time to market
mcqs.explanation: Production partnerships allow firms to pool complementary expertise and resources, speeding up product development. The other options describe unrealistic or extreme consequences that do not normally result from such partnerships.
